summary: At family-runtime 104ff465 / HEAD cae1c860 the v2 declarative compiler has gained bounded ordinary-ERC20 multi-output effects and an address-surface reverse-binding declaration, but a faithful set-redemption JSON is still impossible. The Basic action and fragment contract cannot be expressed: declarative fragments are always exactly one runtime-program node, while the family contract requires one direct redeem(set,amount,recipient) calldata node plus one assert-balance node per positive basket output. Basket execution is still a single flat register program, not the family's nested execSubscript chunking, so the 9+-component baskets (the family supports 187) and the external-recipient direct-settlement path fail the declarative register budget. Discovery still selects exactly one nomination channel, while the family combines address-surface binding with receipt-log fallback and uses a custom reverse-binding provider. Both lineages and all three owned actions therefore remain on the handwritten TypeScript production entry.

unblockRequirement: A public framework change is required before a faithful set-redemption JSON can exist: (1) add a direct-ABI action declaration with a runtime amount patch and preserve the family action encode/matchTrace semantics; (2) let a quoted fragment declare one action node plus per-basket-output assert-balance nodes, or provide an equivalent JSON node-list declaration; (3) provide a nested runtime-program execution composition (execSubscript/run equivalent) with the existing 16-register/128-instruction/64KiB bounds, including direct-settlement side-output preservation; (4) allow one discovery declaration to compose address-surface nomination + receipt-log fallback + the implemented reverse-binding provider; (5) preserve both lineages and all three actions. Alternatively the family contract/tests could be changed to accept a single runtime-program fragment and a weaker fragment node shape, but public TS/tests are out of scope and that would not preserve the current interface.
